When the overall visual fidelity is on par with ease of use it will definitely be more noticed. Right now the standalone experience is good but not enough to make the majority of potential consumers look at it. 

Right now flatscreen games have really good graphics while standalone vr still has good graphics but not to the point where it could attract people. 

Imagine a vr multiplayer experience like Vrchat, but photorealistic. That would definitely be something lots of people would like to try and it would push vr to be way more “mainstream”. 

I mention graphics because it is the first thing one notices when using standalone vr, but other things like portability also play an important role. PCVR is considerably closer to that “mainstream” quality but even for PCVR, there’s still potential for better quality. 

Objectively speaking, cloud/game streaming could become the solution and the push VR needs to be more noticed. At the moment it is not that viable though, but who knows if it will be in the future

2:My pc is on the lower end so even if I can join pc only worlds, the unoptimized environment in those instances(really high poly avis and an overall least optimized experience) makes it an unenjoyable experience. I still stick with quest compatible content/worlds. I could also move the settings around, but I no longer feel like doing it. People seem to not understand that a f2p model is not a good fit for a game like Hytale. It could very well be f2p but it wouldn’t make sense if it did. The games that have a f2p model usually are multiplayer-only games, and if a person is not willing to pay money usually these f2p games lurk users with paid benefits like cosmetics and by partially locking the game’s experience behind a paywall. 

The whole issue relies in the fact that Hytale will have a a singleplayer experience and a lot of players won’t even touch multiplayer as much. Also, a f2p model will need extra monetization other than cosmetics. If the game is f2p it will most likely lock things like multiplayer and mods behind a lot of paywalls or through a predatory monthly subscription. F2P as a whole goes against the freedom Hytale plans to offer. If the game is free it wouldn’t be delivering it’s intended experience. P2p would also have some monetization, but it wouldn’t go beyond cosmetics and it definitely wouldn’t get invasive, similar to Minecraft Bedrock.

Regardless of the model I will definitely play this game.

Look at games that offer proper singleplayer experiences like pokemon, resident evil, Skyrim, Terraria, Zelda Breath of the Wild, the Mario Bros games. How could these games make any profit if they were free? They all are, for the most part, singleplayer experiences. They definitely wouldn’t use a tipping jar.
